newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index scores record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index scores record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index ended the last day of trading under colonial rule at a record closing high but its gains paled in comparison to the red chips which were bid sharply higher ahead of a new era under China.
The China-Affiliated Corporations Index surged 224.63 points, or 6.92 percent, to 3,469.32 while the blue chip Hang Seng Index gained 68.77 points, or 0.45 percent, to 15,196.79.
"Very interestingly it is the red chips which have had a very, very strong day and the more traditional blue chips were lagging," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston.
"Behind the facade of the market -- in a way you can look at it as the old market -- there were some very big movers today."

While the Hang Seng Index scored a record closing high, beating the previous record close of 15,154.36 points registered on June 20 this year, the red chip index notched up its biggest gains since it was launched on June 16.
Traders on the stock exchange floor cheered on Friday as the closing bell rang for the last time under British rule.
Among the biggest gainers of the day were the new Chinese powerhouses which are expected to see a bright future when Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on Monday.
Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd surged HK$3.90 to HK$48.20 and China Resources Enterprise Ltd gained HK$3.10 to HK$38.00.

The most heavily traded stocks of the session were largely red chips. Blue chips Hopewell Holdings Ltd and Hang Seng Bank Ltd appeared on the list on speculation that the new era under China may bring mainland shareholders into the companies.
Hopewell rose HK$0.15 to HK$4.90 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$2.50 to HK$110.50.
Property stocks limited the Hang Seng Index's gains. It had reached a high of 15,275.54 points in early trade, just 46.79 points shy of its all-time intra-day record of 15,322.33.

With Hong Kong's new government expected to announce its future housing policy soon after the handover and the U.S. Federal Reserve due to meet next Tuesday and Wednesday, some investors approached next week's handover holiday with caution.
The market will be closed from Monday through Wednesday.
Old British "hong" Swire Pacific Ltd fell HK$1.50 to HK$69.75 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd fell HK$1.25 to HK$68.75.
Jiangsu Expressway Co Ltd, the last initial public offering under colonial rule, closed at HK$2.75 compared with an issue price of HK$3.11.
Friday's total turnover was a heavy HK$26.02 billion.
